title: Opening hours, blocks and shifts
moduleTitle: App: Field service operations (proposed module; not in curriculum/structure yet)
audience: Owners and office staff who schedule, dispatch and record field jobs. No developer knowledge is needed.
learningOutcomes: Set working hours for a worker or an area, including time slots.
Choose between regular working hours and a shift for a given pattern of cover.
Explain how a shift's status changes what the scheduler uses.

instruction.heading: Opening hours and time blocks
instruction.body: Working hours tell the scheduler when a worker or an area can take a visit. This same record type can also capture a customer's arrival window or time preference, which makes it useful in several ways. A time slot carves out a block inside those hours, such as a morning block set aside for one type of job. Hours can be set for an area, and a worker's own hours can override them. Keep hours realistic, because the scheduler treats them as fixed until someone changes them.

instruction.heading: Shifts for irregular cover
instruction.body: A shift suits work that does not follow a fixed weekly pattern, such as on-call duty, overtime or a contractor who works an agreed set of days. A shift runs from a beginning to a finish in the area's time zone, and it may name an area, a worker and a status. A tentative shift is still being planned. A published shift is ready to hand to the worker. A confirmed shift has a named worker, and the scheduler takes confirmed shifts into account. A shift can also be marked as extended time, meaning it falls outside normal working hours.

procedure: Set the normal working hours for each area, and for each worker whose hours differ from the area.
Add time slots where a type of job needs a fixed block, such as an early start.
Create shifts only for dates where cover is irregular.
Set each shift to tentative, published or confirmed according to what the worker has agreed.
Check that every confirmed shift names a worker, and that the worker belongs to the shift's area if one is set.

workedExamples.situation: A carpet cleaner works Tuesday and Friday as usual, but covers an on-call Saturday every fourth week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you change the regular hours or add a shift?
workedExamples.reasoning: Regular hours describe the usual pattern. The Saturday cover is irregular, so it belongs in a shift. Confirm it only once the worker has agreed to it.

equipmentAndPpe: A device with the SkilledAt.Work Field app, where the lesson uses it

commonErrors.error: Setting a shift to confirmed before any worker is named.
commonErrors.prevention: Only confirm a shift after a worker is attached to it.

commonErrors.error: Setting a worker's hours to differ from their area without a reason.
commonErrors.prevention: Add a short note explaining why the hours differ.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers app records and office process only. It does not grant, confirm or replace any licence, certificate or authority, and it makes no legal claim.
